item.research_question: Can a new Zr-Ti-Nb alloy be developed with a low Young modulus suitable for biomedical application?
item.material_system: Zr-Ti-Nb alloy with a composition of 59.57-19.02-21.41 mass%
item.processing_route: Vacuum-arc melting process with further forging-rolling treatment
key_findings: Extremely low Young modulus of 27.27 GPa for the alloy and 34.85 GPa for the bar
Tensile strength of 900.1 MPa after post-casting treatment
Full biocompatibility demonstrated by cell culture experiment
Uniform distribution of Zr, Ti, and Nb within the new alloy
Low modulus alloys have shown better osseointegration in the early postoperative period
item.mechanism: The low Young modulus of the Zr-Ti-Nb alloy is attributed to the formation of a β-phase and the combination of Zr, Ti, and Nb
item.future_work: Further experimental and clinical evidence and more investigations of β-zircon alloys for dental implant manufacturing are still required
quotes: an extremely low Young modulus with adequate tensile and yield strength and elongation parameters
the mechanical properties of the new alloy in the deformed state correspond to grade-5 Ti, but the elastic modulus is much closer to that of natural bone
the cell culture experiment demonstrated full biocompatibility, indicating that the new alloy could be used for dental and orthopedics implant production

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a new Zr-Ti-Nb alloy be developed with a low Young modulus suitable for biomedical application?. System: Zr-Ti-Nb alloy with a composition of 59.57-19.02-21.41 mass%. Processing: Vacuum-arc melting process with further forging-rolling treatment. Test conditions: Tensile test, cell culture experiment. Findings: Extremely low Young modulus of 27.27 GPa for the alloy and 34.85 GPa for the bar; Tensile strength of 900.1 MPa after post-casting treatment; Full biocompatibility demonstrated by cell culture experiment; Uniform distribution of Zr, Ti, and Nb within the new alloy; Low modulus alloys have shown better osseointegration in the early postoperative period. Mechanism: The low Young modulus of the Zr-Ti-Nb alloy is attributed to the formation of a β-phase and the combination of Zr, Ti, and Nb. Future work: Further experimental and clinical evidence and more investigations of β-zircon alloys for dental implant manufacturing are still required. Quote: "an extremely low Young modulus with adequate tensile and yield strength and elongation parameters"
